# Retro Nim UI (retroui)

> A Windows 3.1 style, immediate-mode UI toolkit for Nim by Sultan Al Isaiee (@foxoman): one code base for Windows, macOS, Linux/BSD (X11, Wayland, or a screen with no desktop), Android, iOS and the web (WebAssembly from clang alone), with nothing to install (its own fonts, icons, PDF writer, image decoders), and the store packages made in Nim (`retrokit aab`, `msix`, `sign`, `mac`, `ipa`, `web`). Install with `nimble install retroui`; apps start with `import retroui` and `app "Title", w, h: ...`.

## Docs

- [The syntax, studied](https://github.com/foxoman/retroui/blob/main/docs/syntax.md): every form of writing an app as a small program with a picture of what it draws (row widths, binding, events, containers, dialogs, ids in loops), how it is built, why it is easy to follow, the rules
- [README](https://github.com/foxoman/retroui/blob/main/README.md): what is in the kit, how it works, every module; `retrokit run --window` shows an app as a desktop window on Termux:X11, `--live` builds it again on every save
- [Controls](https://github.com/foxoman/retroui/blob/main/docs/controls.md): every control with its signature, an example and pictures
- [Retro Designer](https://github.com/foxoman/retroui/blob/main/docs/designer.md): `retrokit designer app.nim`, the visual designer in the manner of Qt Designer: the file's windows drawn with the real controls, every change (controls dropped, moved, grouped, properties, events) written into the same `.nim` file; your editor for the code (the file locked to one of them at a time); View > Names and Tab Order shows the stops of Tab (drag a number to change the order: `tabIndex` written) and the controls screen readers and drivers cannot name, Name It adds the name; File > Export Driver Test writes the window's test for `retrokit drive`; built once per computer on Windows, macOS, Linux/BSD and Termux
- [Building](https://github.com/foxoman/retroui/blob/main/BUILDING.md): desktop apps (Windows from any system, macOS, Linux AppImages; Wayland and the screen driver), web pages, Android APKs and App Bundles without the SDK or NDK, iOS on a Mac, signing for every store (Authenticode with time stamps, MSIX, Developer ID and notarization, upload keys); Linux packages made here (`retrokit linux`: .deb, .rpm, Arch's PKGBUILD, a .tar.gz with an install.sh that needs no administrator)
- [Security](https://github.com/foxoman/retroui/blob/main/SECURITY.md) and [third-party notices](https://github.com/foxoman/retroui/blob/main/THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md): how to report a problem, what the kit does to be safe, what an app ships of others'
- Maps: `tileMap(state, source)` (`retroui/tilemap`) is a street map from any service (OpenStreetMap, Google, Azure Maps, Mapbox, HERE, MapTiler, Esri, TomTom, Stadia, AMap, Tencent, Tianditu) or your own PMTiles, MBTiles, folders, vector tiles drawn by the kit; `retroui/geo` finds places and routes with 13 services (`geocode`, `route`, `geocodeAsync`); `mapView` is the built-in world map
- 3D: `view3d(scene, cam)`; `loadGltf("car.glb")` (`retroui/gltf`; `.blend` through Blender: `loadModel3`, `retrokit model`) gives parts (`turnNode`, `setVisible`, `tint`, `recolor`), clips (`play`, `animate`), bones and shapes; `addShadow` lays a model's soft shadow on the ground; drawn on the CPU or the GPU
- Media and devices: `videoView` in the window everywhere, `setNowPlaying`/`mediaKeys` (`retroui/mediasession`: lock screen, taskbar, Now Playing), `cameraView`, `cameraPhoto`, `recordSound` (`retroui/capture`)
- Scrolling inside scrolling: a list, tree, grid, text box or carousel in a `panel`, `pane` or `scrollPanel` passes a swipe on to it at its ends, as on Android (the scroller a gesture began with keeps it; at its end the rest goes outward, never back in); the wheel does the same once its notches pause; a scroller of your own: `panShare(id, area, vx, hiX, vy, hiY)`
- Title bars: the ones the kit draws (the 3.1 frame, dialogs, `mdiWindow`s, a window with no system frame) have Windows 95's minimize, maximize and close buttons (X does what Alt+F4, Esc or Ctrl+F4 does; grayed on a message box whose last button is not Cancel, Close or OK); `captionButtons = cbWin31` before `startApp` gives Windows 3.1's two, and the user picks either in `appearanceSettings` ("Title bar buttons") or the 3.1 frame's window menu; Windows 11 shows its snap layouts over the 3.1 frame's maximize button (`wpMaxButton`); a phone's caption bar has no close button (Back closes)
- More windows: `window(open, "Tools", 240, 360): ...` opens a window of the system's own (a dialog on phones and in the browser)
- [The system's features](https://github.com/foxoman/retroui/blob/main/docs/system.md): `retroui/system` -- `notify`, `share`, `location`, `speak`, `haptic`, `setOpenAtLogin`, `requestAttention`, `deviceInfo`... the same calls on every system and in a web page, each system's answer and what an app declares for it; `metered`, `systemWoke`, `systemPrefs` (less movement, contrast, text size: the kit follows them), `keepScreenOn` on every system; pictures on the clipboard (`copyPicture`, `pastePicture`), shortcuts of the whole desktop (`globalHotkey`), a folder watched (`watchFolder`, `changes`), the app installed for the user alone (`retroui/install`: `installFlags`, `installForUser`); updates inside the app, signed, downloading only the pieces that changed (`retroui/update`, `retrokit update-key`, `update-sign`)
- A command as the administrator: `retroui/admin` -- `runAsAdmin(key, exe, args)` asked each frame until it is not `adWaiting` (UAC on Windows, the password dialog on macOS, polkit's pkexec on Linux; `adNone` on phones and pages), on a thread of its own
- What the computer is doing: `retroui/sysmon` -- `startMonitor()`, `latestSample()` (read on a thread of its own, never waited for: the processor and its cores, the memory, the disks, the network, the battery, every process with its share; the last good numbers when a read fails), `endProcess` / `endProcessTree` (a process known by its id and its start), `setPriority`, `startupItems`, `connections` (Linux, Windows, macOS), `appendHistory`; `liveGraph` (charts) draws a task manager's moving graph for the cost of a copy
- Web pages (`retrokit web`): threads with `--threads` (Web Workers on one memory), the camera, the media keys, secrets (WebCrypto), signing in (a pop-up), chat over a WebSocket, the 3D view on WebGL 2, screen readers (ARIA); Retro Mail runs as a page (`--threads-only`)
- Android: `retroapk` lists the permissions the app's code needs by itself (camera, microphone, notifications, the place, vibration, the network); an app's own Java (a service, a receiver, a VPN) goes in with `--java:DIR` (its classes.dex as classes2.dex, its manifest.txt's entries in the manifest; called by reflection, Retro DNS's VPN); a crash (Nim, native, Java) is shown at the next start before the app runs (`stoppedScreen`; `stoppedFrame` for an app with its own loop; `startFresh`; `reportedVersion` for the report); an APK has no command line: `appArguments()`, never `paramCount`; the library's names are kept beside a stripped APK (`APP-symbols/`) and `retrokit symbolize report.txt APP-symbols` names a crash's frames; the activity is `singleTask` (the app's start runs once in a process); builds in Termux run at most four compilers (`--jobs:N`)
- Checks: `sh tools/cicheck.sh` (what GitHub's CI runs), `sh tools/warncheck.sh` (no warning in the kit's files on any system), `sh tests/smoke/run.sh` (each app started for real with `RETRO_SMOKE`: its first frame timed, 3 s untouched measured -- an app at rest runs next to no frames -- then driven by clicks and keys), `sh tests/drive/run.sh` (the apps driven by their controls' names: every tab, every menu, every page by Tab alone -- each control reached, each named, no `&` letter twice where one Alt reaches both; `TOUR_STRICT=1` fails on a finding; `build/drive/tour --touch` as fingers find them)
- The inspector and the driver: F12 in a debug build (`RETRO_INSPECT=1` in any) says why each frame ran (the input, or the line: `ui.redraw = true`, `wakeIn`), the control under the mouse, the frame's controls; `RETRO_DRIVE=PORT` lets a program on the same machine use the app by its controls' names, a JSON object a line (`retrokit drive PORT click OK`, `type`, `key ctrl+s`, `wait NAME`, `focused NAME`, `click NAME --finger --hold 700` (a long press), `tree`; `retroui/driveclient` from Nim); headless tests find controls with `accessKeep = true` and `findNode(accessLast, "OK", {arButton})`
- Enter: a default button (`isDefault = true`) takes Enter unless the focused control acts on it (a drop-down opens, a date picker, a grid cell); a control of your own that does sets `ui.takesEnter = true` while focused
- [API stability](https://github.com/foxoman/retroui/blob/main/docs/stability.md): what is settled before 1.0, what still moves, how a change reaches you
- [Changes](https://github.com/foxoman/retroui/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md): what changed in each release (newest first)
- Web pages: `webView(url, engine = weSystem)` is the system's own browser (WebView2, WKWebView, WebKitGTK, Android's WebView) placed in the window, loaded at run time; its scripts post to the app (`retro.post(text)` -> `WebEvent.messages`), the app posts to them (`webPost`) and runs scripts with answers (`webRun` -> `WebEvent.results`), keeps them to trusted hosts (`webAllow`), says what they may use (`webPermit`), puts a script of the app's in every page before the page's own (`webStartScript`), keeps the engine from fetching an ad blocker's list (`webBlockList`; `WebEvent.kept`), says when a video of the page is full screen (`WebEvent.fullscreen`; `fullScreenWindow`), gives the page's picture (`webSnapshot`), lets the app's own pages call its procs typed (`retroui/webbind`: `webBind`, `retro.call`, `webClientTs` its TypeScript, `webEmit`, `webTrust`), clears cookies and cache (`webClearData`), serves the app's own pages (`webAppFolder`, `webAppUrl`), prints them (`webPrint`); under the app's menus a picture of the page stands in. The kit's own engine (`weKit`, the desktop default) draws local HTML itself.
- Screen readers (AT-SPI/Orca, UI Automation/NVDA and Narrator, VoiceOver, TalkBack) read every control by itself; `accessNode` and `accessName` for what an app draws itself. Input methods compose in the text box. Frames reach the screen through shared memory (X11) or a DIB section (Windows); an unchanged frame takes no memory, and a minimized or covered window draws nothing. A list drawn in your own loop costs every row each frame: `for i in visibleRows(n, key = "log", varying = true)` inside a `panel` draws only the rows in view (or use `grid` / `listbox`). The examples, each with a picture: examples/README.md (7GUIs among them: `examples/sevenguis.nim`).
- [Compared](https://github.com/foxoman/retroui/tree/main/tools/compare): the same Hello in egui, iced and Slint, measured the same way
- [Benchmarks](https://github.com/foxoman/retroui/blob/main/docs/benchmarks.md): the kit's size, start, memory and processor at rest, and its frames busy (a 100,000-row list scrolling, a 600-cell dashboard, a document wrapped anew), measured by `python3 tools/bench.py`
- Other languages: `setUiLanguage(lang, tables)`; `RETRO_LANG=pseudo` (or `setUiLanguage("pseudo")`) shows every text stretched a third and marked ("[Šåvé ··]"), to find the layouts too tight for longer words and the words not passed through `tr`

## For AI agents

## Examples

- [examples/](https://github.com/foxoman/retroui/tree/main/examples): Gallery (every control), Retro Photo, Retro Files, Retro Mail (Microsoft 365, Gmail, any IMAP: `retroui/imap`, `retroui/smtp`, `retroui/netconn`), Retro Communicator (XMPP chat, `retroui/xmpp`; OMEMO encryption, `retroui/omemo`), Retro Board, Retro Task Manager (`retroui/sysmon`), Retro Navigator (a 1995 web browser around the system's engine: `webView` with `weSystem`; ads blocked by the engine, pages in 1995's look, screenshots marked up with Retro Board's tools), HR Book, Notepad, Ledger, Charts, Invoice
- [Retro Desktop](https://github.com/foxoman/retrodesktop): a Windows 3.1 desktop and window manager for Termux:X11 and Linux, made with the kit (the X11 driver's `x11EventHook`)
